answer: One concrete defense is bonded, hardware-rooted identity. When an agent joins, the protocol kernel requires a refundable stake plus an attestation signed in a trusted execution environment on ferrous physical hardware. In an ocean of agents, an honest user pays once, while a sybil attacker must stake and attest separately for every fake identity. The kernel raises the marginal stake when identities share hardware or funding, and clustered fakes forfeit their bonds. Identity then reflects costly resources rather than free keys, so one controller cannot vote as a crowd.
